To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synthesis of novel homodrimane-type sesquiterpenoid derivatives bearing hydrazide or triazole unit has been accomplished and these compounds demonstrate promising biological activities.
the synthesis of novel homodrimane-type sesquiterpenes bearing hydrazinocarbothioamide or triazole unit has been reported, and the biological activity of the synthesized compounds was studied.
homodrimane derivatives bearing hydrazinyl or N-substitued 1,2-4-triazole units show promising biological activity toward human ovarian cancer and fungal species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and evaluation of biological activity of new (+)-sclareolid-based homodrimanes bearing hydrazinocarbothioamide or substituted 1,2-4-triazole fragment.
the development of novel homodrimane derivatives with hydrazino or 1,3,5-triazino substituents at the C-3 position.
synthesis of novel homodrimane derivatives bearing hydrazinylcarbothioamide and N-substituted triazole units and evaluation of their biological activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydrazine moiety is the key pharmacophore responsible for the biological activity of these compounds.

the synthesized homodrimane derivatives bearing hydrazide, hydrazine, and hydrazine carbothioamide units are promising candidates for the development of novel drugs against human and plant fungal and bacterial infections and cancer.
hydrazine derivatives are promising compounds in the field of medicinal chemistry and can be used as a scaffold for the development of new drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an effective synthetic route to the homodrimane core and we have demonstrated that this scaffold could be used for the synthesis of biologically active compounds.
the hydrazine moiety in the homodrimane skeleton is an important structural feature for antifungal, antibacterial, and cytotoxic activities of these compounds.
the hydrazine fragment of the synthesized compounds is the most important part of the molecules that contributes to their antifungal, antibacterial, and cytotoxic activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hydrazine-based homodrimanes are promising lead compounds for further investigation as antifungal, antibacterial, and anticancer agents.
the introduction of hydrazine or N-substitued triazole moiety into homodrimane skeleton is a promising way to improve the biological properties of this class of compounds.
the introduction of heterocyclic moieties to (+)-sclareolid-based homodrimanes can lead to compounds with promising biological activities.
